AarPreviewRead.description:
What the report will hold, before it exists: whether a session it
can start from has been held, whether the caller may start it, and the
objectives it will cover.
AarPreviewRead.title: AarPreviewRead

AarRunChangeRequest.description: Write the report from another session (`revision` as in a save).
AarRunChangeRequest.title: AarRunChangeRequest

AarRunOption.description:
A session the report can be written from: the current one or an
archived one.
AarRunOption.title: AarRunOption

AarSaveRequest.description:
The whole report in one save (autosaved). Objectives are the plan's
-- only their text and level change; actions are full-replace keyed by
id. `revision` is the one the client edited.
AarSaveRequest.title: AarSaveRequest

AbsenceFallback.description: What happens if a key decision maker can't attend.
AbsenceFallback.title: AbsenceFallback

ActorFields.description: What an actor is, at any level of the library.
ActorFields.title: ActorFields

ActorInput.description:
A simulated actor. `id` is set for a saved row; `key` is how injects
in the same payload refer to it -- the id itself for a saved row, any
temporary string for a new one (same scheme as the needs form).
ActorInput.title: ActorInput

ActorOrigin.description:
Where a simulated actor comes from -- the actor library's levels.
An exercise's cast only holds copies; the origin says of what.
ActorOrigin.title: ActorOrigin

AllowedDomainTagAssignmentRequest.description:
Full-replace semantics, same shape as PlannerTagAssignmentRequest
-- the ids in this list are exactly the tags that should end up
assigned to this allowed-domain row.
AllowedDomainTagAssignmentRequest.title: AllowedDomainTagAssignmentRequest

ArtifactKind.description:
How the Playground renders an inject's content as a simulated
artifact (a template drawn by the app, never uploaded markup).
ArtifactKind.title: ArtifactKind

AttackAttribution.description:
Whose activity an inject's ATT&CK techniques are: a threat actor of
the scenario's, or noise -- unrelated activity (other attackers,
commodity malware, coincidences, false positives) that tests the
players' triage. None (the column null): no ATT&CK at all.
AttackAttribution.title: AttackAttribution

AttackConversionRead.description:
What moving references onto another ATT&CK release changed: MITRE's
replacements applied (techniques and groups) and what that release
doesn't have.
AttackConversionRead.title: AttackConversionRead

AttackRef.description:
An ATT&CK technique under the tactic it serves, by id. Whether it
exists is checked against the MSEL's pinned release by the service
(the payload doesn't carry the release).
AttackRef.title: AttackRef

AttackRefRead.description:
With its names in the pinned release (English, as MITRE publishes
them) -- kept in snapshots, so a frozen MSEL reads on its own.
AttackRefRead.title: AttackRefRead

AttackReleaseRead.description: GET /attack/{version}: one release, what the picker offers.
AttackReleaseRead.title: AttackReleaseRead

AttackUpgradeRead.description:
POST /ttx/{ttx_id}/msel/attack-upgrade: the MSEL on the new release
and what changed on the way.
AttackUpgradeRead.title: AttackUpgradeRead

BareRegisterRequest.description:
A brand-new account with no organization and no invitation token --
pending role assignment (an org grants Planner later, or the user
redeems a token later). Mirrors RedeemAccountCreate/ProgramManagerCreate's
field shape/validators exactly.
BareRegisterRequest.title: BareRegisterRequest

Capability.description: Capabilities an exercise can validate -- TTX-Zone's own taxonomy.
Capability.title: Capability

CatalogImageRead.description:
An illustration of a catalog inject, served at
GET /inject-catalog/{id}/images/{index}?lang=; copied into the MSEL
with the inject.
CatalogImageRead.title: CatalogImageRead

ConductPrepContext.description: What the plan is checked against, read-only here.
ConductPrepContext.title: ConductPrepContext

ConductPrepSaveRequest.description:
PUT /ttx/{ttx_id}/conduct-prep -- the whole plan in one save, like
the MSEL: a DRAFT may be incomplete (the validation report judges it),
collections are full-replace keyed by id, `revision` is the one the
client edited.
ConductPrepSaveRequest.title: ConductPrepSaveRequest

CopySender.description:
Who sends it, when it isn't already in the cast: found there by its
TTX-Zone id or its name, or added as a copy.
CopySender.title: CopySender

DashboardWeeklyAccess.description:
Access granted in one week: to Players, and to the exercise team
(planning and control team, Evaluators, Observers) -- an exercise's
creator, who gets in by creating it, isn't counted.
DashboardWeeklyAccess.title: DashboardWeeklyAccess

DefaultContextRequest.description:
Login-time default context. All three optional; null means "use the
first available one". See organization_service.set_default_context.
DefaultContextRequest.title: DefaultContextRequest

DomainAccountRead.description:
An account from one of the organization's allowed domains that holds
no role in it yet.
DomainAccountRead.title: DomainAccountRead

EEGDuePhase.description:
A phase the objective (or one of its decisions) is due by the end
of -- its deadline, from the MSEL.
EEGDuePhase.title: EEGDuePhase

EEGExpectedAction.description:
An MSEL expected action, listed under each objective its inject
evaluates -- an observation point with its window.
EEGExpectedAction.title: EEGExpectedAction

EEGPoint.description:
An observation point of a definitive EEG (the conduct prep's), with
what each rating level means for it.
EEGPoint.title: EEGPoint

EEGRead.description:
The Exercise Evaluation Guide (EEG): what evaluators observe and
rate. Deliberately *not* the design -- no needs, risks, sponsor, scope
or stop keyword -- since the Evaluator role has no access to it.
EEGRead.title: EEGRead

EegObjectiveInput.description:
The points of one definitive EEG. EEGs themselves aren't created or
removed by a save -- they follow the needs analysis' objectives (the
re-seed adds and drops them).
EegObjectiveInput.title: EegObjectiveInput

EegPointKind.description:
Where an observation point came from: a clause of the objective's
success criterion, an expected action of the READY MSEL, a notification
requirement the objective cites, or written here.
EegPointKind.title: EegPointKind

EmailInvitationAccountCreate.description:
A new account for the invited address (the address comes from the
invitation, never from the form).
EmailInvitationAccountCreate.title: EmailInvitationAccountCreate

EmailOutboxRead.description: A queued or sent message, without its content.
EmailOutboxRead.title: EmailOutboxRead

EmailReconfirmationRead.description:
Platform -> Email -> Periodic reconfirmation: after how many days
every account confirms its address again (None: never).
EmailReconfirmationRead.title: EmailReconfirmationRead

EmailSettingsRead.description:
Platform -> Email. Never carries a secret: `has_password` says
whether one is stored, `password_readable` whether the current key
still decrypts it.
EmailSettingsRead.title: EmailSettingsRead

ExerciseActorInput.description: One actor of an exercise's cast, written from Templates.
ExerciseActorInput.title: ExerciseActorInput

ExerciseInjectAddedRead.description:
POST /ttx/{ttx_id}/msel/injects: the MSEL, and what moving the copy's
techniques onto its ATT&CK release changed.
ExerciseInjectAddedRead.title: ExerciseInjectAddedRead

ExerciseInjectInput.description:
POST /ttx/{ttx_id}/msel/injects: one inject added to the MSEL -- a
copy of a library inject, already in the exercise's language with its
variables filled in. The MSEL's own save rules apply afterwards (the
validation report judges it; nothing here needs to be complete).
ExerciseInjectInput.title: ExerciseInjectInput

ExerciseJoinRequest.description:
A Program Manager taking a seat on an exercise themselves: as
ExercisePersonAddRequest, for the caller.
ExerciseJoinRequest.title: ExerciseJoinRequest

ExercisePersonRead.description: One row of the exercise's people matrix.
ExercisePersonRead.title: ExercisePersonRead

ExerciseScenarioRead.description:
What an exercise holds today, and whether a scenario may replace it
(a played exercise keeps the design its sessions ran).
ExerciseScenarioRead.title: ExerciseScenarioRead

ExerciseThreatActorAddedRead.description:
POST /ttx/{ttx_id}/msel/threat-actors: the scenario's new threat
actor, and what moving it onto the MSEL's ATT&CK release changed (a
group that release doesn't have is in `removed`: the actor stays, as an
unknown actor).
ExerciseThreatActorAddedRead.title: ExerciseThreatActorAddedRead

ExpectedNotificationRead.description:
A notification regime the team should recognise during the session
(services/notification_reference.py): derived from the notification
requirements the objectives cite.
ExpectedNotificationRead.title: ExpectedNotificationRead

FindingKind.description: What a review found wrong with the design.
FindingKind.title: FindingKind

FindingSource.description:
Which review of the design found it: the sponsor's or another
stakeholder's review of the drafts, the Final Planning Meeting or the
dry run.
FindingSource.title: FindingSource

FrozenVersionRead.description:
A version of the MSEL frozen when it became READY, and the sessions
played from it.
FrozenVersionRead.title: FrozenVersionRead

ImprovementFollowUpRequest.description:
How an action is going: never reopens a FINAL report. The re-test
link changes only when `retest_ttx_id` is sent (null clears it).
ImprovementFollowUpRequest.title: ImprovementFollowUpRequest

InjectArtifact.description:
An inject's content rendered as a simulated artifact. The body is the
inject's own `content`; these are the template's other fields, whose
meaning follows `kind` (email: from, address, to, subject, date; press
release: outlet, dateline, headline, date; social post: author, handle,
date; chat message: sender, channel, date). All plain text: the
Playground draws them, nothing is ever rendered as markup.
InjectArtifact.title: InjectArtifact

InjectFamily.description:
The kind of threat an inject belongs to; `regulatory` and `generic`
are transversal (they serve any scenario).
InjectFamily.title: InjectFamily

InjectFileInput.description: An uploaded file of the MSEL handed out with the inject (in order).
InjectFileInput.title: InjectFileInput

InjectFormat.description:
What an inject is, and so what it asks of the table: an inject that
evaluates objectives (INJ), a discussion slide -- a debrief or reflection
prompt, no objective, not in the EEG nor the coverage (DSC) --, or a poll
the Players vote on, outside the evaluation too (POL).
InjectFormat.title: InjectFormat

InjectImageInput.description: An uploaded image of the MSEL shown with the inject (in order).
InjectImageInput.title: InjectImageInput

InjectStage.description: Where in the incident an inject sits -- the MSEL's suggested phases.
InjectStage.title: InjectStage

InstancePolicyRead.description:
What the menus need, signed in or not: whether an account may found
an organization on its own (signup, avatar menu, Waiting Room).
InstancePolicyRead.title: InstancePolicyRead

LegalAcceptanceItem.description:
One version of one document the user accepts (signup, or after a
substantial change). Must be the version currently published.
LegalAcceptanceItem.title: LegalAcceptanceItem

LegalDocumentAdminRead.description:
Platform's view of one document: the working draft, whether it differs
from what's published, and every published version.
LegalDocumentAdminRead.title: LegalDocumentAdminRead

LegalDocumentKind.description:
The legal documents a deployment's operator publishes for its users
(Platform), accepted together at signup.
LegalDocumentKind.title: LegalDocumentKind

LegalDocumentSummary.description: The latest published version of a document, without its text.
LegalDocumentSummary.title: LegalDocumentSummary

LegalTemplateRequest.description: The operator's details, written into the templates once.
LegalTemplateRequest.title: LegalTemplateRequest

LibraryAttackUpgradeRead.description:
POST /organizations/{id}/{threat-actors,injects}/attack-upgrade: how
many of the organization's library items moved to `attack_version`,
and what changed on the way.
LibraryAttackUpgradeRead.title: LibraryAttackUpgradeRead

LibraryDeleteResult.description:
`deleted`: gone for good. `disabled`: still in use, so it was
disabled instead; `usage` says where.
LibraryDeleteResult.title: LibraryDeleteResult

LibraryUsageExercise.description: An exercise holding copies of the item.
LibraryUsageExercise.title: LibraryUsageExercise

LibraryUsageInject.description: An inject of the library sent by the item (an actor).
LibraryUsageInject.title: LibraryUsageInject

MeterInput.description: An impact meter: what the polls' decisions add up on.
MeterInput.title: MeterInput

MfaPolicyFields.description:
Whether each role must have a second factor. The instance
administrator always must, so it has no field.
MfaPolicyFields.title: MfaPolicyFields

MselFilePreviewRead.description:
GET .../files/{file_id}/preview: the beginning of a text file as plain
text (never rendered as markup). `truncated` when the file goes on past
`limit_bytes`.
MselFilePreviewRead.title: MselFilePreviewRead

MselFileRead.description:
POST /ttx/{ttx_id}/msel/files: the stored file, to link from an
inject (`InjectFileInput.file_id`).
MselFileRead.title: MselFileRead

MselImageRead.description:
POST /ttx/{ttx_id}/msel/images: the stored image, to link from an
inject (`InjectImageInput.image_id`).
MselImageRead.title: MselImageRead

MselRenumberRead.description:
POST /ttx/{ttx_id}/msel/renumber: the MSEL and the codes it had
(row id -> code), which undo sends back.
MselRenumberRead.title: MselRenumberRead

MselRenumberRequest.description:
Renumber one kind of row in order -- or, to undo, put back the
`codes` (row id -> code) a previous renumbering returned.
MselRenumberRequest.title: MselRenumberRequest

MselRoomRead.description: A room of the exercise, as the MSEL aims injects at it.
MselRoomRead.title: MselRoomRead

MselSaveRequest.description:
PUT /ttx/{ttx_id}/msel -- the whole MSEL in one save, like the needs
form: a DRAFT may be incomplete (the validation report judges it), only
what can never be stored is rejected (unknown references, limits), and
collections are full-replace keyed by id. `revision` is the one the
client edited (optimistic locking).
MselSaveRequest.title: MselSaveRequest

MyAccessRequestRead.description:
A player's own view of one of their access requests -- unlike
TTXAccessRequestRead (a Planner's admin view of who's asking), this
carries ttx_name/organization_name instead of the requester's own user
info, since the viewer already knows who they are.
MyAccessRequestRead.title: MyAccessRequestRead

MyLeaveRequestRead.description: A Player's own pending request to leave an exercise.
MyLeaveRequestRead.title: MyLeaveRequestRead

MyRoleInvitationRead.description: An offer as the invited account sees it.
MyRoleInvitationRead.title: MyRoleInvitationRead

NeedInput.description:
A needs-analysis row. `id` is set for a row that already exists
(kept, so objectives and future links survive edits); `key` is how
objectives in the same payload refer to it -- the id itself for an
existing row, any client-chosen temporary string for a new one.
NeedInput.title: NeedInput

NeedsContext.description:
What the MSEL needs from the needs analysis to be edited: the
objectives to link, the participants recipients must be (M09: the
participating areas and, optional, the third parties), the duration
limit and the TLP it inherits. Nothing else of the form.
NeedsContext.title: NeedsContext

NeedsFormRenumberRead.description:
POST /ttx/{ttx_id}/needs-form/renumber: the form and the codes it
had (row id -> code), which undo sends back.
NeedsFormRenumberRead.title: NeedsFormRenumberRead

NeedsFormRenumberRequest.description:
Renumber needs in creation order or objectives in needs order -- or, to undo, put back
the `codes` (row id -> code) a previous renumbering returned.
NeedsFormRenumberRequest.title: NeedsFormRenumberRequest

NeedsFormSaveRequest.description:
PUT /ttx/{ttx_id}/needs-form -- the whole form in one save. A DRAFT
may be incomplete: completeness is reported by the validation report,
and only the rules that can never hold in a stored form (V01, V02, V04)
reject the save. `revision` is the one the client edited (optimistic
locking). Collections are full-replace, keyed by id.
NeedsFormSaveRequest.title: NeedsFormSaveRequest

ObjectiveTemplateRead.description:
GET /objective-catalog -- one SMART objective template, both locales.
`criterion_*`/`evidence_*` hold one line per entry (the form joins them).
ObjectiveTemplateRead.title: ObjectiveTemplateRead

OidcPublicConfig.description: What the sign-in page needs to offer single sign-on.
OidcPublicConfig.title: OidcPublicConfig

OidcSettingsRead.description:
Platform -> Single sign-on. Never carries the client secret:
`has_client_secret` says whether one is stored, `client_secret_readable`
whether the current key still decrypts it.
OidcSettingsRead.title: OidcSettingsRead

OrgMemberExerciseRead.description: One exercise of the organization the person is on, and as what.
OrgMemberExerciseRead.title: OrgMemberExerciseRead

OrgMemberRead.description:
One person in Admin -> Users and roles: every grant they hold in the
organization, and their tags (one set per person).
OrgMemberRead.title: OrgMemberRead

OrgMemberTagsRequest.description: Full-replace semantics, applied to every grant of the person.
OrgMemberTagsRequest.title: OrgMemberTagsRequest

OrgRoleInvitationCreateRequest.description:
Admin -> Users and roles -> Add person where roles are offered, not
granted (organization_role_invitation_service).
OrgRoleInvitationCreateRequest.title: OrgRoleInvitationCreateRequest

OrgRoleInvitationRead.description:
An offer as its organization's Program Managers see it: the address
they typed, never anything about an account.
OrgRoleInvitationRead.title: OrgRoleInvitationRead

OrganizationAllowedDomainUpdateRequest.description: The domain name itself isn't editable -- remove and re-add instead.
OrganizationAllowedDomainUpdateRequest.title: OrganizationAllowedDomainUpdateRequest

OrganizationFoundRequest.description: A signed-in account founding an organization of its own.
OrganizationFoundRequest.title: OrganizationFoundRequest

OrganizationInjectFields.description:
What an inject template is in an organization's library: one
language, stated in `language`. See OrganizationInject.
OrganizationInjectFields.title: OrganizationInjectFields

OrganizationLeavePreviewRead.description: What leaving the organization would take (Preferences -> Privacy).
OrganizationLeavePreviewRead.title: OrganizationLeavePreviewRead

OrganizationProfileUpdateRequest.description:
Program Manager-editable organization profile fields, past signup --
tax_id lives here rather than on OrganizationProfileCreate, since it's
a Program Manager org-settings concern, not a registration-form field.
`name` is optional so a client that omits it leaves the name unchanged;
when sent it's stripped and must not be blank.
OrganizationProfileUpdateRequest.title: OrganizationProfileUpdateRequest

OrganizationRead.description:
Not built via automatic from_attributes conversion (despite the
model_config below, kept for the id/name/tax_id/subscription_tier/
created_at fields that do map 1:1 onto the Organization model) --
`logo_url` has no matching attribute on Organization (only
`logo_path` does, see organization_logo_service.logo_url), so every
call site constructs this explicitly, field by field.
OrganizationRead.title: OrganizationRead

OrganizationScenarioCreateRequest.description:
Add a scenario to the organization's library, from exactly one
source: a TTX-Zone scenario, another of the organization's (a
duplicate), or one of its exercises.
OrganizationScenarioCreateRequest.title: OrganizationScenarioCreateRequest

OrganizationSummary.description:
One organization a user belongs to, from their own point of view --
used for the org switcher and the default-organization preference, not
to be confused with OrganizationRead (the org's own admin-facing
profile). is_program_manager/is_planner come strictly from
OrganizationMembership, mirroring core/security.py's own helpers of
the same name -- a Player-only or per-TTX-Planner-only org
still appears here (see list_user_organizations), just with both flags
False.
OrganizationSummary.title: OrganizationSummary

OrganizationTagApplyRequest.description:
Full-replace semantics, same shape as TTXTagAssignmentRequest --
the ids in this list are exactly the tags that should end up applied
to the Organization; every other tag in this org's pool becomes
unapplied.
OrganizationTagApplyRequest.title: OrganizationTagApplyRequest

PlannerOverviewRead.description:
Creator -> Exercises for a Planner: organization-wide counts, and the
Program Manager's panels over the Planner's own exercises only (never
another manager's exercise names).
PlannerOverviewRead.title: PlannerOverviewRead

PlannerTagAssignmentRequest.description:
Full-replace semantics, same as TTXTagAssignmentRequest -- a
dedicated class rather than reusing that one directly since this
validates against a different tag table (OrganizationTag, not
TTXTag).
PlannerTagAssignmentRequest.title: PlannerTagAssignmentRequest

PlanningTeamFunctionsRequest.description: Full-replace of a member's functions on the exercise.
PlanningTeamFunctionsRequest.title: PlanningTeamFunctionsRequest

PlayerOption.description:
A Player with access to the exercise: when they used the invitation
(`invited_at`, None if they were added another way) and when access
was granted (`joined_at`).
PlayerOption.title: PlayerOption

ProgramManagerRead.description: Same shape as a Planner grant: the user plus the grant's tags.
ProgramManagerRead.title: ProgramManagerRead

RatingLevel.description:
The common rating scale: performed without challenges (P), with
some (S), with major ones (M), or unable to be performed (U).
RatingLevel.title: RatingLevel

RegulatoryFrameworkRead.description:
A framework a regulatory trigger can name; OTHER isn't one (it's
implied, always offered last, with free text).
RegulatoryFrameworkRead.title: RegulatoryFrameworkRead

RetestCandidate.description:
A later exercise of the organization that can re-test an action:
its code, name and objectives -- nothing else of it.
RetestCandidate.title: RetestCandidate

RetestRead.description:
The later exercise that re-tests an improvement action, and which of
its objectives (none: the exercise as a whole).
RetestRead.title: RetestRead

RetestRequest.description:
A Program Manager links an action to the exercise that re-tests it
(both null: unlinked).
RetestRequest.title: RetestRequest

RetestedAction.description: An improvement action of an earlier exercise that this one re-tests.
RetestedAction.title: RetestedAction

RiskTemplateRead.description: GET /risk-catalog -- one exercise risk template, both locales.
RiskTemplateRead.title: RiskTemplateRead

RoleEnum.description:
TTX-scoped roles: PLANNER is a member of the exercise's planning and
control team (what they do on it -- plan, control, facilitate -- is in
the row's flags); EVALUATOR rates the exercise with the EEG and
OBSERVER watches it, neither with access to the design; PLAYER plays
it.
RoleEnum.title: RoleEnum

RoomTeamMemberRead.description:
A team member who follows the session, and the room their view of it
opens on (null: the main room). They can still look at any room.
RoomTeamMemberRead.title: RoomTeamMemberRead

RoomsRead.description:
Creator -> Exercise -> Rooms: whether the exercise uses rooms, its
rooms and its Players with their seat.
RoomsRead.title: RoomsRead

RunActionRead.description: An expected action of an inject and what the Controller saw of it.
RunActionRead.title: RunActionRead

RunDecisionRead.description: A decision of the table's log, as recorded (and maybe edited).
RunDecisionRead.title: RunDecisionRead

RunDecisionWrite.description:
A decision of the table. `inject_code` defaults to the inject in
play; `room_code` is the room a team member records it in (a Player's
is where they are).
RunDecisionWrite.title: RunDecisionWrite

RunEndexRequest.description: The closing message to the table, as the Controller words it.
RunEndexRequest.title: RunEndexRequest

RunEvaluationRead.description:
The evaluator's EEG for the session: the objectives they rate (all
of them for the Lead Evaluator) and how far along they are.
RunEvaluationRead.title: RunEvaluationRead

RunFacilitationRead.description:
The Facilitator's script for the phase in play: its key questions
(and which were put to the table) and the inject's facilitator notes.
RunFacilitationRead.title: RunFacilitationRead

RunFeedbackFormRead.description:
The participant feedback form, in the caller's language: open once
the session is over, answered once.
RunFeedbackFormRead.title: RunFeedbackFormRead

RunFeedbackResultsRead.description:
What the participants answered, aggregated and unsigned. Under
`minimum` answers only the count shows, so no one can be singled out.
RunFeedbackResultsRead.title: RunFeedbackResultsRead

RunFeedbackWrite.description: Statement key -> 1..5 and open question key -> text; all optional.
RunFeedbackWrite.title: RunFeedbackWrite

RunInjectRead.description: A delivered inject, safe for the Players.
RunInjectRead.title: RunInjectRead

RunMeRead.description: A Player's own seat and where the Controller has them now.
RunMeRead.title: RunMeRead

RunMeterGroupRead.description:
The meters of one place: the table, or a room (`room_code`; null, in
rooms: the main room).
RunMeterGroupRead.title: RunMeterGroupRead

RunMetersShown.description: Show the impact meters' summary to the Players, or hide it.
RunMetersShown.title: RunMetersShown

RunMilestoneRead.description: A step after the session, dated from it by the plan's calendar.
RunMilestoneRead.title: RunMilestoneRead

RunMoveRequest.description:
Players to the main room or back to their own: these, a room's, or
(neither given) everyone.
RunMoveRequest.title: RunMoveRequest

RunNoteWrite.description:
The note on an inject (`inject_code`) or the general one (""): its
whole text -- empty deletes it.
RunNoteWrite.title: RunNoteWrite

RunPastRead.description: An archived run of the exercise, for the list of previous runs.
RunPastRead.title: RunPastRead

RunPhaseRead.description: A phase as the table sees it: its name only once it has begun.
RunPhaseRead.title: RunPhaseRead

RunPointRead.description:
An observation point to rate: what it means at each level (blank:
the common scale), where it comes from, what the Controller saw of its
expected action, and the evaluator's rating.
RunPointRead.title: RunPointRead

RunPollClose.description:
Closing a vote; `record_option` records that option as a decision,
`outcome_option` is the one whose consequence the table gets.
RunPollClose.title: RunPollClose

RunPollRead.description: A question put to the Players' vote: the tally, never who voted.
RunPollRead.title: RunPollRead

RunPollResults.description: Show a closed planned poll's result to the Players, or hide it.
RunPollResults.title: RunPollResults

RunPollWrite.description: A question for the Players' vote, on the inject in play.
RunPollWrite.title: RunPollWrite

RunPresenceRead.description:
Someone on the Playground right now. A Player sees the other
Players by name, and only how many of each role the team is.
RunPresenceRead.title: RunPresenceRead

RunProjectRequest.description: The delivered inject to show in the main room; null clears it.
RunProjectRequest.title: RunProjectRequest

RunQuestionPlaceRead.description:
In rooms, each place asks and covers a phase's key questions on its
own: the positions, like `released_questions` and `covered_questions`.
RunQuestionPlaceRead.title: RunQuestionPlaceRead

RunQuestionsRequest.description:
Key questions of a phase (by position) to put to the table on the
inject in play.
RunQuestionsRequest.title: RunQuestionsRequest

RunRatingWrite.description: A level, or none to withdraw the rating.
RunRatingWrite.title: RunRatingWrite

RunRealWorldRequest.description: REAL WORLD: the exercise's stop keyword, typed to confirm.
RunRealWorldRequest.title: RunRealWorldRequest

RunReleaseRequest.description:
A contingent inject needs the reason it fires; a mandatory one may
carry one (released early or late, say).
RunReleaseRequest.title: RunReleaseRequest

RunRoomPlayerRead.description: A Player and where they are (the Controller's view, to move them).
RunRoomPlayerRead.title: RunRoomPlayerRead

RunRoomsRead.description:
An exercise played in rooms. A Player gets only their own room (and
the injects of it and of the main room); the team gets every room and
every delivered inject; the Controller also each Player, to move them.
RunRoomsRead.title: RunRoomsRead

RunSummaryRead.description:
How the session went, for its Controllers, Planners and Lead
Evaluator: time played, injects, expected actions, key questions,
ratings, notes -- and what comes after, dated.
RunSummaryRead.title: RunSummaryRead

ScenarioActor.description: A simulated actor of the cast (who plays it is left out).
ScenarioActor.title: ScenarioActor

ScenarioApplyRequest.description: Overwrite the exercise with a library scenario.
ScenarioApplyRequest.title: ScenarioApplyRequest

ScenarioCheck.description:
The outcome of checking a document against a target, with nothing
written (a dry run) -- or of the import itself. `ok` false: errors were
found and nothing changed. `replaces`: what the target holds today and
an apply would overwrite.
ScenarioCheck.title: ScenarioCheck

ScenarioFile.description:
An inject file, embedded (base64) byte for byte, with its SHA-256

info.description:
The HTTP API behind TTX-Zone's web application. Every path is under `/api/v1`.

It may change between versions while TTX-Zone is 0.x: there is no compatibility promise yet.

## Authentication

The API uses the web application's session: `POST /auth/login` sets a session cookie and a
CSRF cookie. Requests that change something must repeat the CSRF cookie's value in the
`X-CSRF-Token` header. Sessions expire, and sensitive operations need a recent authentication
(`POST /auth/step-up`), answering 403 `REAUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` otherwise.

The AI assistant's `/mcp` endpoint is the exception: it takes a personal access token as a
bearer token.

## Context

Requests name their organization or exercise in the path or the body. The server never infers
them.
info.title: TTX-Zone API
